A 17-year-old high school student accidentally amputated part of his right index finger during shop
class. His teacher applied dressings and pressure to the wound and transported him to the emergency
department within 20 minutes of the incident. The patient’s medical history includes asthma, and his
only medication is albuterol. Vital signs show a temperature of 98.0°F (36.6°C), blood pressure of
103/66 mmHg, pulse of 111/min, and respirations of 20/min. Examination reveals pulsatile bleeding
from a clean-cut wound at the distal interphalangeal joint of the right second finger. The wound was
cleaned, compression applied, analgesics given, and hand surgeons were notified. The amputated
finger was left in the classroom, but the principal is bringing it to the hospital. What is the proper
method for transporting the amputated finger? Answer Choices: (A) Wrap the finger in moist gauze and
place in a plastic bag (B) Rinse the finger with hydrogen peroxide, wrap the finger in moist gauze, and
place on ice (C) Rinse the finger with tap water, wrap in moist gauze, and place directly on ice (D)
Wrap the finger in dry gauze, place in a plastic bag, and submerge the bag in ice water (E) Rinse the
finger in sterile water, wrap in dry gauze, and place directly on ice (F) Submerge the finger in sterile
saline and place the container on ice (G) Place the finger in a sealed plastic bag without rinsing and
keep it on ice (H) Rinse the finger in normal saline, wrap the finger in moist gauze, put in a plastic bag,
and place the bag in ice water (I) Rinse the finger in normal saline, place in a dry plastic container, and
keep at room temperature (J) Submerge the finger directly in ice water
 A. Submerge the finger directly in ice water
B. Rinse the finger in sterile water, wrap in dry gauze, and place directly on ice
C. Rinse the finger in normal saline, place in a dry plastic container, and keep at room temperature
D. Wrap the finger in moist gauze and place in a plastic bag
E. Submerge the finger in sterile saline and place the container on ice
F. Wrap the finger in dry gauze, place in a plastic bag, and submerge the bag in ice water
G. Rinse the finger with hydrogen peroxide, wrap the finger in moist gauze, and place on ice
H. Rinse the finger in normal saline, wrap the finger in moist gauze, put in a plastic bag, and place
the bag in ice water

I. Rinse the finger with tap water, wrap in moist gauze, and place directly on ice
J. Place the finger in a sealed plastic bag without rinsing and keep it on ice
